title: A Partitioning-Based CAD Flow for Interposer-Based Multi-Die FPGAs
problem: Multi-die interposer-based FPGA architectures face limited inter-die connectivity resources and increased interposer delays compared to intra-die routing, which directly impact routability, routed wirelength, and maximum clock frequency.
motivation: Effective partitioning and routing for multi-die FPGAs is critical to overcome the inter-die communication bottleneck and maintain performance in modern FPGA designs.
method: The approach presents FPGAPart, a timing-driven netlist partitioner tailored for FPGA designs, integrated with VTR 7.0. It leverages VTR's pre-packing solutions as clustering hints and uses the FP-Growth algorithm to detect frequently occurring patterns across timing paths for enhanced clustering. Neighborhood influences-based cutting planes are introduced into the core ILP solver to achieve significant runtime speedup with minimal solution quality degradation.
key_novelty: FPGAPart is the first open-source timing-driven netlist partitioner designed specifically for FPGA architectures, incorporating neighborhood influences-based cutting planes for 38× faster ILP optimization with <1% quality loss.
contributions: FPGAPart: First open-source timing-driven netlist partitioner for FPGA designs handling architectural constraints
Integration with VTR 7.0 using pre-packing solutions and FP-Growth pattern detection for clustering
Neighborhood influences-based cutting planes achieving 38× ILP runtime speedup with <1% solution degradation
Demonstrated ~3% routed wirelength and Fmax improvements vs VTR 7.0; up to 7% Fmax vs hMETIS/METIS/TritonPart

metrics.speedup: 38× ILP solver speedup; ~3% rWL and Fmax improvement vs VTR 7.0; up to 7% Fmax vs competing partitioners
metrics.other: <1% solution quality degradation despite 38× runtime speedup
